judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble is a straightforward identification of parties, but it treats "Fund" and "Plan" as interchangeable labels for the same thing, which is a latent definitional slippage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 1.20 and 1.22 carefully distinguish the "Plan" (the rules) from the "Trust Fund" (the assets), so the preamble's equation of the two sits awkwardly with Article 1; Amendment No. 4 also replaces this preamble entirely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short recital in ordinary language; nothing in "establish the Plan and require periodic Employer contributions" carries two readings on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the CBAs "establish the Plan," whereas Section 1.20 and Section 4.2 make the Plan a set of rules adopted and amended by the Board, a mild recital-versus-operative tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely narrative recital about what the CBAs contemplate; no operative term to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 3 in fact has the Association (not the Union) appoint Employer Trustees and the Union appoint Union Trustees, so the recital's shorthand is imprecise but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Exclusive purpose of providing pension and retirement benefits" is a familiar formula, though "exclusive" is doing real work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2 says "certain pension and related benefits" and Section 5.3 charges administrative expenses to the Fund, so the recital's narrower "exclusive purpose" is slightly out of step with the operative text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dated historical recital of the trustees' intent to restate; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.2's definition of the Agreement as amended and restated from time to time.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital cites "Paragraph 18 of the Trust Agreement" as the amendment power, a citation that has no counterpart in the restated instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The operative amendment power is Section 10.1 (with the provisos in 10.1(a)-(c)) and Section 10.2; a recital pointing to a vanished Paragraph 18 is a classic recital-versus-operative mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration boilerplate with no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the instrument turns on this recital of consideration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The "unless the context otherwise requires" qualifier lets any defined term be displaced by context, which is a small but real source of interpretive play.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 12.7, which imports Plan definitions "except as otherwise expressly provided," giving two overlapping definitional priority rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining "Administrator" as "the Board, or any individual or other person duly authorized by the Board" is broad but not genuinely ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.6 makes the Board the ERISA "administrator" while Section 7.1 (garbled) contemplates an Administrator distinct from the Board, so the two roles blur.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional cross-reference to the instrument itself; plain and self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the preamble and Section 10.1's amendment mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition names the "Publishers' Association of New York," dropping "City" from the entity's actual name — a small mechanical slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble, Section 12.8(d) and the signature block all say "Publishers' Association of New York City," so the defined term does not match the party as named elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Both the Chairman and Secretary of the Board" leaves open whether they must act jointly or each qualifies alone, and the trailing "(or their duly authorized agents)" widens the class further.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.15 requires the Chairman and Secretary together to execute documents while Section 12.6 makes an instrument signed by the Chairman alone conclusive, so who is truly "authorized" is not uniform across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition defers to "the terms of the Plan" for who qualifies, which is definite even if it is not self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.2 and Section 12.15, which likewise make Plan terms controlling for entitlement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise definition tied to ERISA sections 402(a)(2) and 3(16)(A); little room to argue about its wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes the Board the ERISA "administrator" while Section 1.1 and Section 7.1 create a separate "Administrator" office, a mild overlap of roles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The defined "Code" is the "Internal Revenue Code of 1936," which does not exist; the intended reference is plainly 1986, a mechanical error in a term used throughout.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.3, 4.4, 10.1(b) and 5.7 all hinge on Code sections 401(a), 501(a) and 4975, so an incorrect Code year ripples through the instrument, though the correction is obvious.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Or other written agreement between an Employer and the Union, which is in force and effect and is acceptable to the Board" makes the category turn on an unstated standard of acceptability.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.13 defines Employer by reference to a CBA and Section 2.4 requires an approved CBA, so whether an unapproved agreement creates an obligation to contribute is left circular.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is long but definite; the incorporation "to the extent not inconsistent with the terms of this Agreement" is a standard priority rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Board's disclaimer of liability for Collective Trust trustees sits alongside Section 5.7's prudence duty and Section 7.2(13)'s duty to monitor, a familiar tension but not a squarely stated conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Containing at least one Employer Trustee and one Union Trustee" is a clear minimum requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.6(b) requires each Committee to have "an equal number of Employer Trustees and Union Trustees," which forbids compositions that Section 1.10's minimum would permit — a direct inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: coverage turns on employment plus a CBA requiring contributions for the individual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Sections 1.13, 2.4 and 9.1, all of which key obligations to the CBA.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition folds two distinct roles — Corporate Trustee and custodian — into one term joined by "and/or," leaving the Custodian's status uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.12 speaks of the Corporate Trustee as a separate sole trustee while Sections 5.12 and 8.1(b) treat the Custodian as a mere holder, so the merged definition does not map onto how the term is used.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any employer required to contribute" is circular in that the obligation is what defines the class, but the CBA reference gives it content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.4 makes participation depend on executing a Board-approved CBA and designating an effective date, so whether a non-signatory can be an "Employer" is not resolved between the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference definition; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3(a) is amended by Amendment No. 4, but the definition tracks whatever 3.3(a) says.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard statutory definition; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently throughout; ERISA supremacy is also confirmed by Sections 2.3 and 12.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined entirely by reference to ERISA section 404(b) and 29 C.F.R. 2550.404b-1; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5(p) uses the term consistently with the same regulatory requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Able to verify with a reasonable degree of certainty the identity of the sender" is a soft standard, but it is a familiar one and the core requirement (signed writing) is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with Section 1.4's Authorized Person definition and Section 8.6's Instructions; no conflict appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully enumerated (a)/(b)(1)-(3) qualifications tracking ERISA and the Advisers Act; little interpretive play.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states that an Investment Manager "has acknowledged in writing" fiduciary status, whereas Section 8.3 makes obtaining that acknowledgment merely permissive ("may require").

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple segregation definition; "segregated by the Trustees" is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.1(b) has the Board or the Custodian do the segregating, a trivial variance rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: the Plan is the Board-adopted rules on eligibility and benefits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble equates "Fund" and "Plan," and Recital 2 says the CBAs establish the Plan, both slightly at odds with this Board-adopted-rules definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All Trust Fund securities of any and every kind ... including, but not limited to" followed by eleven enumerated categories is the paradigm general-catch-all-against-specifics structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5 grants powers over "Securities or other property," so the breadth of the definition is largely absorbed by the parallel "other property" language elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear asset-based definition covering segregated and pooled holdings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 1.9, 1.19, 5.1 and 5.12; the only friction is the preamble's use of "Fund" to mean the Plan.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical "(if such Successor Trustees have been appointed)" and the phrase "when acting as Trustees" are awkward and leave the successors' status conditional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.11 vests successors with full powers on acceptance, so the conditional definition is at most redundant rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "And any affiliates thereof" is an undefined extension of the party's identity, though the named local is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble also uses "affiliates" collectively, so the instrument is internally consistent even if the boundary of "affiliates" is soft.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to Section 3.3(b); nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.8 and 3.10 add that Union Trustees are the Union's incumbent officers, which supplements rather than contradicts the definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line naming provision with no operative reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same name appears in the preamble and Section 9.3; no divergence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Certain pension and related benefits" leaves the boundary of "related benefits" undefined while the sentence is framed as an "exclusive purpose."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Recital 4 says the exclusive purpose is "pension and retirement benefits," and Section 4.1(a) permits "such other related benefits as the Board may from time to time determine" — three formulations of the same limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming language — anything inconsistent with the Code or ERISA means "this Agreement shall be deemed amended in such fashion as will implement the purposes of this Trust" — states no determinate content for the deemed amendment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a whole-instrument override that interacts with Sections 5.9(b), 9.5(b) and 10.1, any of which a party could argue is automatically rewritten by operation of this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any contributing Employer acceptable to the Trustees may participate" makes acceptance discretionary and unstandardised, and the three lettered steps read as conditions without saying they are exclusive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.13 defines Employer without reference to Board approval and Section 2.5 deems obligations onto an Employer, so whether these steps are the only route into the Trust is genuinely unsettled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Shall be deemed to have ... agreed to be bound unconditionally" to all present and future amendments is a strong deeming clause whose trigger is never stated in the section itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.1's closing sentence says nothing in the Trust Agreement changes the terms of any CBA, which cuts against deeming employers unconditionally bound to Board-made amendments imposing new charges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section is misnumbered "3.2" and provides an odd-numbered board — two Employer and three Union Trustees — while the closing sentence points to Section 3.4 for appointment mechanics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.2(b) lets "any four Trustees" call a meeting and Section 10.1(c) forbids unequal voting power, and Amendment No. 4 replaces this text with a two-and-two board, so the composition rule does not sit still across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional acceptance-of-trust clause; the duties it recites are stated elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with Sections 3.4 and 3.11 on written acceptance; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare list of named individuals; nothing to construe in the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 4 replaces this list wholesale, so the original text is superseded rather than inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "As soon as practicable" is soft, but the obligation (file written appointments and acceptances) is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1 says appointment "shall be governed by the provisions of Section 3.4," yet 3.4 addresses only successor appointments, so the cross-reference over-promises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite tenure provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6, 3.7, 3.8 and 6.1(a)'s officer terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence deems a Trustee resigned when "the Contributing Employer which designated him" ceases to contribute, but Trustees are designated by the Association and the Union, not by individual employers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That mismatch runs directly against Sections 3.1, 3.3, 3.7 and 3.9, which vest designation of Employer Trustees in the Association, leaving the deemed-resignation trigger inoperable as written.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Removal "at any time, with or without cause" by written instrument is about as definite as such clauses get.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.6's reference to the "Contributing Employer that designated him" cuts against 3.7's Association-only removal power, a small friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading is "Removal of Union Trustees" but the text mostly prescribes who holds the office, and it supplies no removal mechanism at all except "by operation of law."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.10 says the Union's principal officer designates successors while this section says successors are "elected from the full-time officers," and Section 3.7 gives the Association an at-will removal right with no Union counterpart.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean mechanism: certificate in writing signed by an authorized Association officer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Sections 3.1, 3.3(a) and 3.11 without friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section contradicts itself in one sentence: the principal officer "shall designate a successor Union Trustee by filing ... in which case a Successor Union Trustee shall be elected from the full-time officers of the Union."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.8 (and its Amendment No. 4 replacement) says Union Trustees are automatically the Union's incumbent officers, a third mechanism that cannot be reconciled with either designation or election.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional vesting provision for successors; no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Sections 3.4, 3.9 and 3.10 on written acceptance and filing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is materially incomplete — "Notwithstanding such transfer, the Board ... functions under the Plan" has no verb, and (d) similarly drops words — so the retained-responsibility carve-out cannot be read as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.12 defines the Custodian as the "Corporate Trustee" while 3.12(b) makes the Corporate Trustee a sole trustee of a separate trust and forever discharges the Trustees, which is hard to square with Sections 5.7 and 7.2(13).
